completion_decisions: Register T20 as a four-problem benchmark and comparison-protocol contribution; do not invent a target optimizer.
Do not reproduce the twelve named comparison baselines as T20-owned methods.
Use the input-dependent prose decoder Gc(round(x_i)) because Algorithm 2 step 5 prints the non-input-dependent Gc(i).
Recompute the Jensen wake-decay coefficient from the paper surface-roughness relation and Table-1 constants.
Use candidate-batch parallelism with deterministic indexed writes and a fixed-order best reduction.
missing_information: paper-linked author source code and data archive
author random seeds and run histories
complete result layouts and unrounded numeric outputs
explicit declaration of whether the preceding k=0.086 example or the Table-1 roughness relation controls the four benchmark cases

paper.authors: Tawatchai Kunakote and Numchoak Sabangban and Sumit Kumar and Ghanshyam G. Tejani and Natee Panagant and Nantiwat Pholdee and Sujin Bureerat and Ali R. Yildiz
paper.title: Comparative Performance of Twelve Metaheuristics for Wind Farm Layout Optimisation
paper.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering

paper_source_conflicts.resolution: paper prose controls because it makes the declared decision variables operative
recompute k=0.5/log(h/h0) using Table-1 h and h0

scope.claim_boundary: academic declared reproduction of the four proposed WFLOP problems and comparison interface; not author-code or twelve-baseline numerical replay

constraints_and_repair.resolution: 2000m square boundary and at least 5D spacing; the grid construction makes distinct cells feasible and the all-zero variable-count layout is infeasible

decision_variables.resolution: 100 real variables in [0,1] for variable count; 39 real variables in [1,100] for fixed count

encoding_and_decoder.resolution: round binary variables for Cases I-II; iteratively select and remove Gc(round(x_i)), with the last remaining entry used when the rounded value exceeds the list length, for Cases III-IV

initialization.resolution: not owned by T20 benchmark; the problem interface accepts any conforming population algorithm

metrics_and_repeats.resolution: objective statistics and histories over ten independent runs, Wilcoxon rank-sum test at 5 percent, plus platform physical FES, timing, worker receipt, and scientific hash

objective_and_direction.resolution: minimize Cost divided by average total power

paper_native_cases.resolution: Cases I-II vary count over 100 cells with hub-only/partial overlap; Cases III-IV place exactly 39 turbines with hub-only/partial overlap

parameters.resolution: 10x10 grid over 2000m square, CT=0.88, h0=0.3m, h=60m, D=40m, efficiency=0.4, density=1.225kg/m3, speed=12m/s

stopping_and_physical_fes.resolution: population 100, 250 iterations, maximum 25000 complete physical evaluations per run, ten independent runs

update_order.resolution: candidate evaluations are independent; production writes indexed values in parallel and performs deterministic ordered reduction

wake_power_cost_or_coupled_model.resolution: Jensen linear wake, root-sum-square deficits, cubic turbine power, and either hub-inside-wake or exact rotor/wake circle-overlap fraction

wind_and_scenario_sampling.resolution: 36 directions from 10 to 360 degrees in 10-degree increments at constant 12m/s, averaged for total power

validation.h6_scope: all four problems, 25000 complete 36-direction physical evaluations each, 17 requested and observed workers
validation.h5_scope: independent Python-vs-C++ equation agreement, decoder semantics, exact printed cost, and reconstructed Fig.5/6 layout power within 1.5 percent
